summary: K. R. Norman (1925–2020) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar who studied at Taunton School and Downing College, Cambridge. He held several posts at Cambridge (1955–1992) and edited the Pali Text Society Journal.
K. S. Balasubramanian works in Indology and philosophy. He has served at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as Director (attested 2026).

id: P:K. S. J. M. de Vreese
summary: K. S. J. M. de Vreese (b. 1906) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as a privaat-docent at Leiden University in 1948 and became a professor at the University of Amsterdam in 1960.
K. Sambasiva Sastri (1879–1946) was an Indology scholar. Succeeding T. Ganapati Sastri, he served as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library from around 1925 to 1934.

K. Srinivasan is an Indologist who served as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College. He also held the Brahmasri Anna Subramaniam Chair at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020–2026).
K. V. Puttappa (1904–1994) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He was educated at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, Mysore, and the University of Mysore (~1927–1929).

K. V. Raman (1934–2024) studied at Madras Christian College under A. J. Boyd, the University of Madras, and the Archaeological Survey of India. He worked at the ASI (~1957–1976) and the University of Madras (1955; 1976–1995).

K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary of the Epigraphical Society of India, Director of Epigraphy at the Archaeological Survey of India (1981–1987), and Honorary Director at ORI Mysore (2012).
K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar (1880–1960) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Between approximately 1935 and 1938, he served as Principal of Banaras Hindu University and Central Hindu College.

K. Venkata Ramanan specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Supervised by Yongtong Tang, Sentian Wang, and Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, he studied at Peking University, the Harvard-Yenching Institute, and Visva-Bharati University, where he taught.

id: P:Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso
summary: Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso was a scholar who studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Kaie Mochizuki (b. 1959) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has served as professor of Buddhism (attested 2015) and university president (attested 2026) at Minobusan University.
Kaigen Noritake specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo and served as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaikyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) studied under Kaitei Hayama and Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. An Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he taught at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho universities, and led Shiba High School.

Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934), a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, studied under Ryodo Nukariya, at Komazawa, First Higher School, and Keio. He lectured at Harvard (~1913–1915) and became the first president of Komazawa University (1925–1934).
Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and professor (attested 1999–2002) at Otani University.

Kakichi Kadowaki (1926–2017) was a religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, trained under Sogen Omori, and held a post at Sophia University (~1969–1996).
Kakushō Ujiie (d. 1985) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied abroad at Tribhuvan University. He held a professorship at Koyasan University (attested 1970 and 1984–1985).

Kali Kinkar Datta (1905–1982) was an Indologist and historian. He served as Honorary Director (1959–1966) and Joint Director (1987) of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute and as Vice-Chancellor of Patna University (1973).

Kalidas Nag (1891–1966) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. He taught at Scottish Church College (~1914–1919), Calcutta University (~1923–1955), and was General Secretary of The Asiatic Society (~1942–1946).
